newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon radar contract award upheld.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon radar contract award upheld.

text.p: The General Accounting Office, the investigative arm of Congress, has rejected objections to the award of an airport radar contract to Raytheon Electronic Systems, the company said Tuesday.

The Air Force awarded the contract to Raytheon's electronic systems unit in August. The deal, with a potential value of $619.9 million, calls for the delivery of 213 digital radar units through 2007, the company said.
The award was challenged by other companies that bid for the contract, including Northrop Grumman Corp.
The radar units will provide air traffic services for the Defence Department and the Federal Aviation Administration at many airports across the country, the company said.
A $20 million preproduction contract called for the delivery of up to three airport surveillance radars. It also involved modifying existing systems and testing and supporting the new systems.
The radars provide surveillance of aircraft up to 60 nautical miles and secondary coverage up to 120 nautical miles, the company said.
